deviations: three r186 always creates the WebGL context with alpha: true. Its `alpha: false` option only sets clear alpha to 1, so getContextAttributes().alpha reports true. I pass alpha: false as specified, and the engine also sets canvas.style.backgroundColor = '#000' so the canvas stays visually opaque if any pass writes alpha < 1.

Step clamping: 'RENDER_SCALE_STEPS clamped to the tier's [min, max]' is implemented as unique(clamp(step)). The steps are High [0.75, 0.85, 1], Medium [0.6, 0.67, 0.75, 0.85, 1] and Low [0.5, 0.6, 0.67, 0.75, 0.8]. Low's 0.8 maximum is therefore reachable even though 0.8 is not in RENDER_SCALE_STEPS.

Boot counts as a scale change. lastChangeAt starts at 0, so no step can happen in the first 2 s. This keeps shader-compile and upload hitches from causing an early down-step. A tier change also restarts the 2 s gap.
The revert of a bad up-step is exempt from the 'at most one change per 2 s' rule. Otherwise it could never fire, because the revert window is also 2 s.
'Pinned' means the scale is at the tier minimum while EMA > 1.1x target, held continuously for 2 s. DynamicResolution never returns tierDrop on Low.

Benchmark: while benchmarking = true, samples are collected and the EMA and counters keep running, but scale steps and pinned drops are frozen so the median measures one scale. The spec does not say either way. In timer mode the benchmark median uses GPU ms; otherwise it uses the rAF dt (the same quantity as the EMA).
Hitch guard (not in the spec): each dt and GPU sample is clamped to 250 ms (MAX_DT_MS) before it feeds the clock and the EMA. Without it, one 5 s stall such as a tab switch would force a down-step.

Measurement-source switch (not in the spec): timer mode is used while EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 exists and has delivered a sample within the last 180 frames; otherwise the engine passes null (rAF mode). On every switch the EMA and run counters restart.
Tier regex: 'Basic Render' (Microsoft WARP software rasteriser) is added to the Low list, next to SwiftShader and llvmpipe.
setTier(sameTier) still resets the scale to init and fires both callbacks, per 'quality := preset'.
integration_notes: src/app/composition.ts already calls the API correctly: createEngine(container, {tier}), onResize, onQualityChange, beginFrame before the scene/post render, endFrame after, then updateDynamicResolution(dtMs, shotFrames 30..120). Keep that order. The GPU timer brackets only the work between beginFrame and endFrame, and query results are read one or more frames later in the next beginFrame.

Drawing-buffer size: three's setSize uses Math.floor(cssW * pixelRatio). composition.ts computes bufW/bufH with Math.round, which is 1 px off whenever the product is fractional (for example 1280 * 0.67 = 857.6 gives 858 against a canvas of 857). Use Math.floor or renderer.getDrawingBufferSize() for uViewportH, uPxPerRad and canvasRectPx.
onResize callbacks are not called on registration. composition.ts already calls resize(engine.cssWidth, engine.cssHeight, engine.pixelRatio) once by hand, which is correct.

On a tier change (benchmark drop, pinned drop or setTier) the order is: renderer pixel ratio and size updated, then onQualityChange(q), then onResize(cssW, cssH, pr). Post should rebuild its MSAA target in setQuality or setSize, and strokes.setQuality(q) belongs in the onQualityChange handler.
The engine sets camera.aspect and calls updateProjectionMatrix on every resize, but not camera.fov. The director (M8) owns the fov, including canvasPoseFovDeg(aspect) for narrow viewports.
If beginFrame/endFrame are never called on a GPU that exposes the timer extension, dynamic resolution waits about 180 frames (3 s) before it falls back to rAF deltas.
engine.actionLog, engine.dynamicResolution.lastBenchmark, engine.gpuTimerActive and engine.rendererName are available for the H HUD and the debug overlay.

Headless Chrome rAF is not vsync-locked (about 165 fps), so the real-time runs do not show 60 Hz vsync behaviour. The 17.5 ms rAF up-rule is covered by the unit tests only.

With heavy GPU-bound frames, at most 4 queries are in flight, so some frames have no GPU sample. The heavy run's benchmark had n=71 samples over 91 frames. This is by design (non-blocking), but the median then comes from fewer samples.

deviations: Depth warp, positions: the vertex shader builds every position unwarped (d) and then maps each vertex radially about E to its warped forward depth (stkWarp). Endpoints are identical to the prelude's canvasToWorld(uv, d) under warp, and every other vertex (ribbon edges, spine bow) keeps its exact projection from E. Ribbon width uses the unwarped d before the radial map.

Depth warp, depth test: when uWarpK != 1, log depth (vFragDepth) comes from the unwarped vertex, and gl_Position.z is clamped to the far plane. Without this, k=0 puts every stroke at 1 km (coplanar, so z-fighting) and k=1.6 pushes far strokes to about 6.4e6 m, beyond CAMERA_FAR 600 km (clipped). The warp test was 75% / 38% differing pixels before this change and 0.3-0.4% after it.

Overdraw guards (Lpx, upper fade, near fade dist/Lw) use the unwarped stroke length and distance. They equal the spec values at uWarpK = 1 and are warp-invariant from E. The behind-camera cull still uses the warped endpoints.

Added a vertex LOD: a stroke with Lpx < STK_LOD_PX (20 px) snaps its interior ribbon stations to s=0/1, so the interior triangles become zero-area, and it is drawn flat-profile with no bow. This took the full-budget frame at 720p High on Intel UHD from 115 to 90 ms. Bow and taper are sub-pixel at that size.

Fragment: the bristle amplitude fades as fwidth(w)*nb goes from 0.5 to 1.0 (an anti-alias LOD: a bristle period of 4 px down to 2 px), and the dry-brush step(e, bristle) edge is anti-aliased with fwidth. All derivatives are taken before any discard.

Fragment: vnoise2(vec2(3s, 9seed)) and vnoise2(vec2(18s, seed)) are replaced by a 1-D value noise along s with a per-stroke lane (hash11). The second coordinate was constant per stroke anyway, so this is the same family at half the hashes. bristle(w+0.37) is computed by angle addition.

Fragment: coverage is computed first and the fragment discards before shading (alpha < 0.004 on A2C tiers; alpha < ign on HASHED_ALPHA). Specular is capped at 4. Shading uses a per-vertex bent frame (T and Nb rotated by the kappa bow slope).

UNDERLAYER strokes are placed first inside each chunk and are always drawn: instanceCount = nUnder + ceil(nRest*fraction). This keeps the spec table's UNDERLAYER fraction 1/1/1, which the flag-based design otherwise lost. They render flat: no bristle, impasto, specular, dry brush or outline, W x3, as a ragged lozenge (rounded ends, noisy edge) so they do not read as rectangles.
VORTEX strokes flagged UNDERLAYER get d *= 1.01 in the shader. The shader recomputes VORTEX depth from the arm law, so the generator's '+1%' shell depth (M4) cannot survive otherwise.

RING depth: d = d_k * clamp(recordD/d_k, 0.97, 1.03), or d_k*(1 +/- 0.5% by seed) when the record depth equals d_k exactly. This keeps generator jitter so overlapping ring strokes do not z-fight; the spec says d = d_k.

JET colour ramp in the shader: mix(PAL_CYPRESS_GREEN -> PAL_CERULEAN -> PAL_ZINC_WHITE by sigma), with the record colA/colB as a 35% tint. Emissive = a2.z * sigma, so the generator sets a2.z = 1.1. Depth = jetPoint d * (1 + q3), matching harness/lib/preview.ts.

Storm tumble ordering: T is taken from the endpoints, tumbled by D, and the endpoints are rebuilt about the displaced centre with the same Lw. The spec lists 'tumble' in step 5 before 'T = normalize(PB - PA)' in step 6, so the order was ambiguous.
setCullInflation(extra): radius = baseRadius + extra * dMax * STORM_FIELD_BOUND (2), because |stormField| can exceed 1. The contracts comment says 'radius += extra * dMax'.

Underlay material: polygonOffset(1, 2) is set as specified, but it has no effect once the shader writes gl_FragDepth (log depth). The same push is applied by hand in the fragment shader: a slope term (fwidth of log2 depth) plus a relative distance bias uUlDepthBias = 1e-3. makeUnderlayMaterial gained an optional third parameter, side.

Both stroke and underlay fragment shaders include tonemapping_fragment and colorspace_fragment. These are no-ops when rendering into M9's sceneRT and give correct output when rendering straight to the canvas (harness).
One ShaderMaterial (one program) is shared by all chunks; the spec says 'materials per class group'. Every per-class difference is per-instance or in const tables, so no split was needed.

generateDebugStrokes uses STATIC classes (UNDERPAINT, STAR_CORE, MOON, HILL, HOUSE, GROUND), with depths inside each class's dRange. Solid strokes get a face normal perpendicular to the stroke that faces E (tilt up to 40 deg). Random normals had collapsed one ribbon to a sliver.
contract_requests: Spec 4.3 acceptance 'toggling uWarpK from 0 to 1.6 at E changes no pixel' cannot hold with stock log depth and CAMERA_FAR = 600 km: k=0 makes everything coplanar and k=1.6 puts the underpainting at about 6.4e6 m. M3 works around it internally (unwarped log depth plus far-plane clamp). Any other warped material (M4 dust and backdrop) needs the same treatment or must hide under warp, as underlays do (section 5.3). The spec or contracts should document this.
Consider documenting in contracts.ts that setCullInflation applies a |stormField| bound factor (STORM_FIELD_BOUND = 2), or change the comment to 'radius += extra * dMax * 2'.

Consider adding to the StrokeRecord docs: RING a0.z = ring depth (jitter of 3% or less is honoured); JET a2.z = emissive at the Venus end (1.1) and q3 = relative depth jitter; VORTEX colours stay attached to the stroke while it streams (no recolouring by sigma); UNDERLAYER strokes are always drawn on every tier.

Generators must keep solid strokes inside their face (face normal perpendicular to the stroke direction). Otherwise B = cross(N, T) lies along the stroke and the ribbon collapses to a sliver. Worth a line in contracts.ts next to 'solid'.

known_issues: Performance is far over the spec targets on this laptop's Intel UHD. Full budget (182k strokes): High 1080p 140 ms, High 720p about 90 ms, Low 720p about 34-40 ms, against 16.7 / 22 ms targets. The cost is fragment and fill bound (log depth disables early-Z; sub-pixel slivers each pay for a 2x2 quad). The section 7.1 budget assumes an RTX 5060, which was not available here, so it is NOT verified. The harness's full world also has more HOUSE strokes than budget (33k vs 14k) and generic HILL/GROUND/GROVE fills, so its overdraw is not representative.

Warp invariance is not exactly zero. 0.2-0.9% of pixels differ in some channel, and 0.01-0.04% by more than 24/255 (max 105-164). The remaining sources are edge-sample rounding from different clip coordinates, perspective-correct interpolation on depth-varying strokes, and depth ties between coplanar strokes (harness house walls). I judge this 'dither level', but it is not literally 'no pixel changes'.

Wet highlights are subtle at the spec weights (0.16 * pow(., 28) * imp). They are verified non-zero via STK_DEBUG=2 but barely visible in normal renders. M8/M10 can raise uImpastoGain / uSpecular if more is wanted.

Bristle texture is only visible once a stroke is more than about 40 px wide; below that the anti-alias LOD fades it. At the 720p/1080p canvas pose most strokes therefore read as two-tone tapered ribbons without grooves.

The spec's near fade (smoothstep(0.8, 2.5, dist/Lw)) makes strokes within about 2.5 stroke lengths of the camera transparent. In close macro views this exposes the underlay meshes (shots/strokes-macro.png). This is by design, but camera paths should not linger that close.

The harness generators (funnel, rings, bands, cypress, jet, houses) are simplified stand-ins, not M4-M7. The sparse cypress and visible underlayer blobs in the close shots reflect harness density (2.8k vs 19.5k strokes), not the stroke system.
Not tested with M9's real HalfFloat MSAA sceneRT and EffectComposer; only the default-framebuffer MSAA canvas. A2C behaviour on an MSAA render target is expected to match but is unverified.

No Spector capture was run. There are no per-frame attribute uploads by construction (StaticDraw instanced buffers written once at build; setQuality changes only instanceCount, index/position bindings, uniforms and defines), but this was not measured.
Most screenshots used SwiftShader; only the timing runs used the GPU (ANGLE D3D11, Intel UHD).

VORTEX strokes keep their generator colour while streaming. A stroke born white at the throat re-enters at the mouth still white after wrapping (it fades through the sigma-end alpha window). This follows the spec (no VORTEX recolouring), but the M4/lead should be aware of it.

The vertex LOD (20 px) and the guards use the unwarped stroke. Off-axis under a strong warp (free mode only), the alpha windows describe the stroke as painted, not its warped size, so very large warped strokes near the camera are not faded.

review.exports: Unchanged from the builder's report. strokeBuffer.ts: class StrokeBuffer implements StrokeSink { constructor(capacity = 4096); push(r: StrokeRecord): void; readonly count: number; readonly data: Float32Array; classRange(cls): { dMin; dMax; n }; get(i, out): StrokeRecord; clsOf(i): StrokeClass; flagsOf(i): number }; emptyRecord(): StrokeRecord; it also re-exports buildStrokeLayer, makeStrokeMaterial, makeUnderlayMaterial, makeRibbonGeometry and generateDebugStrokes. strokeMaterial.ts: MAX_CHUNK = 4096; STORM_FIELD_BOUND = 2.7 (was 2); makeStrokeMaterial(u: SharedUniforms, q: QualitySettings): ShaderMaterial; buildStrokeLayer(buf: StrokeBuffer, u: SharedUniforms, q: QualitySettings): StrokeLayerEx. StrokeLayerEx extends StrokeLayer with { chunks: StrokeChunkEx[]; material; drawCalls; dispose() }, and StrokeChunkEx adds { nUnder; center }. ribbonGeometry.ts: makeRibbonGeometry(segments: 3|4|5): BufferGeometry; sharedRibbon(segments). underlay.ts: makeUnderlayMaterial(colorHex: number, u: SharedUniforms, side?: Side): ShaderMaterial; UNDERLAY_DEPTH_BIAS = 1e-3. debugGen.ts: generateDebugStrokes(sink: StrokeSink, rng: Rng, n = 64): void. glsl: strokeVert, strokeFrag.
deviations: Depth warp, changed: the builder overwrote vFragDepth with the unwarped depth but kept perspective-correct interpolation weighted by the WARPED clip w. Varyings across a stroke that spans depths (s, w, and vFragDepth itself) then interpolated differently under warp. That was the main remaining source of warp-invariance error. The vertex shader now rescales gl_Position by wUnwarped / wWarped when uWarpK != 1 (the stroke is not culled and both w > 0). A positive rescale of the clip vector keeps NDC, the pixel and clipping exactly. Interpolation weights and the log depth (1 + w) then become those of the unwarped stroke, so the vFragDepth override was removed. The far-plane clamp z = min(z, w) is kept. Off-axis under warp, the depth test therefore uses unwarped camera distance, the same trade-off the builder chose.
Supersedes the builder's 'Overdraw guards use the unwarped stroke' deviation only for depth and interpolation. The guards themselves are unchanged.

Underlayer strokes now never get an outline: vStkBi.w = outlined && !under ? OUTLINE_W[cls] : 0. The builder's report said underlayers are flat with no outline, but the shader applied OUTLINE_W when a generator set both flags.

STORM_FIELD_BOUND 2 -> 2.7. Each component of the §3 stormField is at most (1.1 + 1.7 + 0.45*2)*0.42 = 1.554, so |field| <= sqrt(3)*1.554 = 2.69. 2 was not a conservative bound, so storm cull inflation could under-cover strokes. The radius is still baseRadius + extra*dMax*bound.

Chunk bounds for sky classes (CLASS_INFO.sky: SKY_BAND, SWIRL, EDDY, STAR_RING, MOON_RING, WIND_JET) now add a stir envelope of 0.05 h-units * 2t * d. The §4.3 step-3 rotation about the cursor moves a point by at most 0.515*z*R, which is 0.041 h for z = 1 and R = 0.08 (§5.3). The builder's bounds had no stir term, which risked culling pops while stirring near the frustum edge.
contract_requests: Same as the builder's first request, updated: the spec's 'uWarpK 0 -> 1.6 at E changes no pixel' needs depth handling under warp (log depth with CAMERA_FAR = 600 km). M3 now does it by rescaling clip w to the unwarped depth, which keeps NDC and makes interpolation and log depth warp-invariant. Other warped materials (M4 dust and backdrop if warped) can use the same 3-line trick: if (uWarpK != 1.0) gl_Position *= wUnwarped / gl_Position.w; then clamp z <= w. deviations: VORTEX across spread is encoded as a fractional arm phase, not q3; all SWIRL/EDDY records have q3 = 0. Reason: the arm law takes depth from sigma only, so an across offset moves a stroke radially at constant depth. Off-axis every arm then became a radial fin and the funnels read as twisted threads (seen at the V6 profile vantage). arm' = arm + 0.2*across/(beta*PI), wrapped into [0, 1.9995]. This keeps r, sigma and depth exactly on the cone d = dThroat (r/r0)^expo. From E the arm band is statistically identical. The funnels now read as continuous flaring horns both in the shared lib preview and through the real M3 material. M3 already decodes arm = q1 - 2*floor(q1/2) and chunks by floor(q1/2).

Shell strokes: arm 0.5/1.5 plus a small on-cone spread (across-equivalent +-0.35). Colours are ultramarine/cobalt over Prussian instead of pure #0b1a3a, which read as black snail-shell bands from E. Shell L = 1.3x the arm law; W = arm-law L/5, and M3 applies x3.
Swirl arm W = L/4 (spec L/5) with L jittered x0.85-1.2, for solidity off-axis (arms are about 1.4 px wide at 55 km).

Swirl colours are not a pure r/rmax ramp. Colours are fixed per stroke while strokes stream through every radius in 24 s, so a radial ramp would slide inward as a hard seam. The ramp position is 0.55*|across|^2 + 0.2*sigma0 + jitter: pale arm cores, cerulean/cobalt edges, edge strokes (|across| > 0.8) 15% darker with the OUTLINE flag, and 8% lemon-tinted whites at the core. Visually stable from E at t = 0, 6 and 90.

Eddies: L = 0.004 + 0.22 r instead of the swirl law; the 0.008 floor would be 1.3 throat radii at r0 = 0.006. W = L/4. No eddy shell, because eddy arms overlap (pitch ratio 1.37). EDDY = 6,000 arm strokes.
Underpaint W = 0.038-0.044 (spec 0.03) with reduced jitter. With 0.03, the M3 ribbon taper (about 0.6 W at the tail) left 0.38% true holes. Now under 0.001%.

SKY_BAND seeding: stratified jittered 2:1 grid, topped up by rejection, instead of pure random sampling. Sky pixels under 3 layers fell from 3.06% to 0.39%. Seeds go down to ridgeV(u,2) - 0.012 (hidden by the hill walls) instead of skyMask > 0.5, which left an underpaint-only strip above the crest.

Star and moon halo areas are NOT excluded from band seeding, per the lead ('leave their halo areas to the band field'). Band directions inside halos (r < 1.25 R) and near vortex discs (r < 1.7 rmax) are blended toward the local tangent, weighted by proximity and radialness. Reason: the band stream cancels the circulation under c1, above c2 and inside halos, leaving only the radial sink, and strokes bristled radially. Swirl throats (r < 1.3 r0) are filled by band strokes curling exactly around the axis in pale swirl colours (a bright eye from E). Eddy eyes (r < 2.5 r0) are band-filled, and the eddy band exclusion is 0.45 rmax instead of 0.7, because eddy throat strokes (about 4 px) fall under M3's lower size fade and left dark holes.

Band colour index uses the band stream function psi = y - 0.022 sin(4x+9y) - 0.012 sin(9.3x-5y+1.7) instead of v, in fract(7*(psi + 0.03 sin(4x))) + 0.1 N(0,1). The stripes then wave with the brushwork instead of lying dead level. Weights are about 0.50/0.34/0.16 (paler within 0.16 above the ridge, deeper above v = 0.88). Two-tone partners: cobalt->ultramarine/#22449e, cerulean->cobalt/#4a77a8, zinc white->cerulean/blue-green.

Deck index b = clamp(round(13 (v - 0.34)/0.76 + 1.8 N), 0, 13), coherent with v so the decks read as shingled tilted strata, not an 85 km-deep confetti volume. dlnd = 12000*dv/d so each stroke lies in its tilted deck. Band direction and kappa come from a 0.0125 h grid of the exact (vortex/halo-aware) direction, bilinear on unit vectors, for the generation budget.

kappa: band/underpaint kappa = 0.5 * turn of the direction over the stroke (the M3 spine law sagitta = 0.25*kappa*L). Funnel kappa is closed-form from log-spiral curvature: -sign(gamma)*0.5*L/(r sqrt(1+beta^2)).

WIND_JET: a2.z = 1.1 for every stroke (the Venus-end emissive; M3 multiplies by sigma). colA/colB are per-filament tints (zinc white / cerulean / blue-green), which M3 mixes at 35% over its sigma ramp.

Backdrop sky splats are a darker continuation of the band field (same band function and pigments, 25% toward Prussian, x0.62, under the HDR 0.6 cap), not 'Prussian-ultramarine with 6% cerulean'. At wide fov near E (shots 4-5) the spec palette made the generated-canvas boundary a hard style seam; it is now only a brightness step.
Backdrop 'earth' is decided from the UNFOLDED direction (below ridgeV in raw v), so looking down from altitude stays ground-coloured instead of mirroring back into sky stripes.

Backdrop u is folded over [0.5 -+ PI/(4 atan(AT))] = [-0.518, 1.518] instead of [-0.3, 1.3]. Two mirror periods then span the full turn exactly, so there is no seam at the atan wrap behind the eye, and the canvas region stays unmirrored. BD_HALF_U/V are generated from atan(AT) and atan(T_HALF). The back-hemisphere 30% contrast is luminance-only, because the RGB-difference version turned pale strokes green.

Dust alpha *= smoothstep(0.03, 0.25, d/|P - C|), the anamorphic apparent-size ratio. Without it, from the shot-8 vortex eye (44 km out) the ~13k motes within 2 km of E piled up additively into a white blob exactly over the village (verified in the real-material render, then fixed).
Dust depth is log-uniform in [50 m, min(250 km, 0.98 * groundHitDepth)], so motes stay above the ground for rows below the horizon.

Dust flow direction for the drift is precomputed on the CPU with the shared TS flowField (attribute aFlow) instead of evaluating flowField per vertex; the values are identical. createDust always builds max(q.dustCount, 30000) points with drawRange = q.dustCount, so a tier change only needs setDrawRange.

deviations: STAR_CORE depth is d_core*(0.99 - 0.0065*hash), not 0.01*hash. With 0.01, Venus cores would reach 11,760 m, outside STAR_CORE dRange [11,800, 16,100]. All cores still sit in front of ring 0.

Ring dash length is L = max(1.3 x spacing, 1.8 x W) for stars and max(1.3 x spacing, 1.6 x W) for the bell. At the spec budgets, 1.3 x spacing alone gives round dots (about 0.004 h), especially for the bell's W 0.006. The dashes now overlap along each ring. Star ring W = clamp(0.85*dRho - 0.08*rho_k, 0.045*rho_k, 0.55*dRho), which fills about 85 % of the radial spacing and leaves thin dark seams. Rows use q3 = {-a, 0, +a} with +-0.4a jitter, so q3 is continuous in [-1, 1] rather than exactly {-1, 0, 1}. a = 1 for stars. For the bell, a = clamp((0.8*dRho - W)/(0.08*rho_k), 0.12, 1), so outer bell rings do not merge into one solid disc. Each dash's value is mottled x0.82 to x1.08.
MOON (crescent) depths are 10,824-10,890 m and the hollow is 10,912-10,978 m, not d = 11,000. Bell ring 0 sits at exactly 11,000, so MOON < MOON_RING would otherwise fail where they overlap.

Moon split: 1,350 crescent strokes and 450 hollow strokes (the spec gives 1,800 total). The hollow is offset 0.40R toward 225 deg with radius 0.80R, so the lit limb is 0.6R thick. Crescent strokes follow the pencil of circles through the two horn points. Colour runs ochre on the inner edge to chrome on the limb, with lemon glints. Bell: chrome overall, but ring 0 is orange (chrome/ochre), ring 1 is pale lemon and the outer ring leans toward lemon / zinc white. The spec says plain chrome; this separates the crescent from its halo.

Cypress centreline: u0_j is spread across [uL + w, uR - w], then soft-clamped (smooth min/max, k = 0.008, 0.0015 margin) to that range. The sway factor is 0.15 for the edge tongues and 0.75 for the next ones, which keeps the E silhouette within 0.01 of CYPRESS_SIL. The spec's taper(v) applies only above the canvas top edge, where each tongue tapers to its own tip at vTop = 1.03-1.17 (y up to about 165 m), converging on u ~ 0.197.

Cypress depth offset dd_j is scaled by clamp(silhouette width / 0.2, 0.3, 1), so tongues converge in depth toward the top (the spec has a constant dd_j). With a constant offset, the thinning upper tongues fanned out along the view ray and opened see-through gaps from the helix pose. Base dd = [-6, 12, -17, 5, 17, -12, 0] +-1.5 m: neighbours differ by at least 12 m, and the sorted depths are at most 6 m apart, so there is no front/back split from the side. Rw uses (192 + dd) instead of 192 so the tubes are truly round.

Cypress shading is baked into colA/colB, because the ribbon shader has no tube normal. Lit = (0.6 + 0.66*(0.5 + 0.5*cos(phi - 0.6))) x per-tongue tone x three helical stripes that follow phi0, so the twist shows. Even tongues lean light (green, 17 % olive) and odd tongues lean dark (80 % #1d2b1f); overall olive is about 10 % and ultramarine flecks 5 %. L = 0.012 + 0.023*sqrt(rand), so lengths stay in [0.012, 0.035] but skew long, and are shortened up to 45 % at the tips.
Cypress seeds cluster per tongue: seed = (j/7 + 0.22*rand) mod 1. The CYPRESS writhe (phase 2*pi*seed) then sways each tongue coherently instead of boiling stroke by stroke.
UNDERLAYER strokes cover the body only (v <= 0.97), and their width is capped at 0.3*w*A so the shader's x3 ribbon never pokes out of the thin tips.

Core lathe follows the silhouette centre at 0.5 x half-width with a +-12 % three-lobe cross-section that twists 2.6 rad per unit v. It closes elliptically between v = 0.72 and the canvas top edge v = 1.0, rather than running to 1.08. Run to 1.08, the smooth core showed between the free flame tips; with the depth convergence and the tubes there, no interior see-through appears.
contract_requests: Soft request to M3, no contract change needed: RING strokes have no per-stroke depth jitter (d = d_k exactly), so the overlapping dashes of one ring are coplanar. I give every ring stroke a random kappa in +-0.3. If the shader honours the spine bow along the camera-facing Nb (section 4.3 step 7), the overlaps get a stable depth order. If M3 does not bow along Nb, please add a tiny seed-based depth offset for RING (for example d_k*(1 + 1e-4*(seed - 0.5))) to avoid z-fighting shimmer while the rings spin.

Optional for M3: the CYPRESS writhe formula keys its phase on seed, which is why I cluster seeds per tongue. If M3 prefers to drive coherent sway from q1 (tongue index), the seed clustering is harmless but could then be dropped.

deviations: Order inside the lens: the radial-smear taps (and the High chroma split) are sampled first from the bloomed input. Isophote banding and the pigment pull then act on the smeared colour. I first followed the spec order (isophote -> pull -> smear) with the smear added as a residual. That turned HDR star cores black at smear 0.8: the residual went negative where banding had darkened a core of about 6. Smear 0 is still an exact no-op.

Isophote banding (define LENS_ISO_DISPLAY, on by default): the spec's multiplier m = 1 + smoothstep(0.35,1.2,Lum)*(0.18*(ring-0.5)+0.1*n) is applied to the tone-mapped peak. The scene colour is then scaled uniformly so its hue is kept. Below the Neutral shoulder this equals the literal c *= m. With the literal scene-referred form, the bands vanish inside the shoulder, which is exactly where the Venus whiteout happens (compare shots/post-punch.png with post-punch-isoscene.png). Brightening is capped at max(peak, 0.99). setLensOptions({isoDisplay:false}) restores the literal form.

Neutral toe pre-compensation (define LENS_TOE_COMP, on by default): the lens adds the exact inverse of the toe offset in three's NeutralToneMapping (x - 6.25x^2, or 0.04) before OutputPass. Below the shoulder, the display is then linear x exposure. Stock Neutral shifts the hues of ultramarine, prussian, cobalt and roof by -3.2 to -5.1 deg (measured in shots/post-swatch-notoe.png), which fails the < 3 deg acceptance. Compensation also makes the matte #0a0b10 and the frame line #3a2a18 display exactly. Side effect: darks are not crushed by Neutral's toe. OutputPass itself is the stock NeutralToneMapping; there is no ACES anywhere.

Added a +-0.5 LSB dither of the 8-bit output before the tone mapper (define LENS_DITHER, on by default). Without it, quantisation alone puts the near-neutral zincWhite swatch 4.9 deg off in hue, and the haze and vignette band.

OKLab pull: the nearest of the 12 pigments is chosen by chromaticity ab/L, which does not change with intensity. The target is that pigment at the pixel's own OKLab lightness, and the weight is mix(c, c', 0.25), or 0.12 when Lum > 1. The pull moves hue and chroma only; HDR values and tonal structure are preserved, and a pigment at any intensity maps to itself.

Weave and varnish are applied only inside canvasRectPx (1 px antialiased edge). Outside the rect, c *= 1 - 0.35*align. Weave: over/under checker with period canvasH/280 and amplitude 0.06*align. It fades out below a 1.4 px period to avoid aliasing (weight 0.89 at a 720 px canvas).

Matte: each bar is solid from its inner edge out to the screen edge. Inner edge = canvasEdge + (1-matte)*(gap + barW), with barW = max(4 px, 0.01*H) as the overshoot, so bars are fully off-screen at matte 0. The frame line is a 2 px band on the bar's inner edge, #3a2a18 at 0.6*matte opacity. Matte, frame and fade (prussian*0.3) colours are display-referred, so they do not change with exposure. The vignette (0.22*r^2, r = 1 at the corners) applies after the matte, following the spec order.

Smear 'over 0.025*smear of the screen radius' is implemented as a zoom blur whose span is 0.025*smear*r, where r is the pixel's distance from the centre. That gives 0.025*smear*R at the corners. Taps are IGN-jittered. Chroma split: R and B taps shifted radially by +-1.5*smear*(r/R) px.
Low tier keeps varnish, outside darkening, dither and toe compensation as well as the listed 4-tap smear, weave, matte and vignette. They are cheap multiplies.

Wire post.setSize(cssW, cssH, pixelRatio) to engine.onResize and post.setQuality(q) to engine.onQualityChange; src/app/composition.ts already does both. Sizes are Math.round(css*pr). three's canvas uses floor, so the two can differ by 1 px; this is harmless.

PostFrame.canvasRectPx must be in drawing-buffer px with y from the bottom. composition.ts's canvasRect(bufW, bufH) with Math.round matches what the harness uses: at 1280x720 the rect is [190, 0, 900, 720], and at 1920x1080 it is [285, 0, 1350, 1080].
post.render() draws the scene into its own sceneRT (renderer.autoClear clears with the renderer's clear colour) and leaves the render target null. Do not call renderer.render to the screen yourself.

The composer targets are HalfFloat with samples 0. sceneRT samples follow q.msaa. setQuality changes the sample count in place (samples = n; dispose(); three rebuilds on next use) and keeps TexturePass's texture reference valid.

Bloom: UnrealBloomPass(threshold 1.0, radius 0.6, strength = f.bloom). It is disabled when f.bloom <= 0. setSize is wrapped so the top mip is bufW*q.bloomScale: 640x360 at High/Medium and 320x180 at Low for a 1280x720 buffer.

The lens uniforms use the uLens* prefix (uLensRes, uCanvasRect, uLensMatte, uLensAlign, uLensSmear, uLensFade, uLensExposure). The lens fragment shader includes GLSL_PRELUDE and spreads the shared uniforms by reference; f.time is not used.
Feature switches for comparisons, e.g. the debug overlay: post.setLensOptions({toeCompensation, dither, isoDisplay, isoRingGain, isoNoiseGain}). Each call recompiles the lens once.
verification: npx tsc --noEmit -p . : 0 errors in src/post/* and harness/post.ts. Errors elsewhere are only other agents' missing modules (src/app/composition.ts imports ../earth/*, ../camera/director).

known_issues: The RTX 5060 budgets (bloom <= 1.0 ms, lens <= 0.7 ms, output <= 0.2 ms) are not verified; no RTX GPU was available. The only measurements are crude headless Intel UHD wall-clock timings (lens ~6 ms on High, ~3.6 ms on Low, bloom 2.4-5.4 ms, all at 1080p). On UHD the post chain alone is a large share of Low's 22 ms frame even at the 0.67 render scale. A real GPU-timer pass is still needed.

In the full emissive test scene, the swatch hue check fails at bloom 0.45 (prussian 7.3 deg, cypressDark 10.5 deg, cypressGreen 4.1 deg, zincWhite 3.9 deg). The bloom haze from nearby stars and windows legitimately adds light to the dark swatches. With bloom 0 the same scene passes (0.06 deg). The acceptance check is therefore enforced only on the isolated strip (scene=swatch).

Test scenes are flat emissive quads, not the real stroke world. The real Venus-punch acceptance at t = 37.6 (rings legible, not a white frame) must be re-checked after integration. In the solid-band stress case 52% of pixels still have luminance >= 235; it is structured into bands but pale.

Toe compensation changes the look relative to stock Neutral: darks are rendered linearly instead of being crushed by the toe. If the lead prefers stock Neutral, setLensOptions({toeCompensation:false}) turns it off, but the < 3 deg palette test then fails for 4 pigments.

The isophote bristle noise is anchored to the screen, so moving or rotating halos will slide slightly under the bristle texture. The value-noise lattice can show rectangular streak blocks where the tangent is axis-aligned; this is visible in the punchwide stress shot.

The weave period is canvasH/280, which is about 2.6 px at a 720 px canvas, close to aliasing. It is faded to 0.89 weight there and disappears below 1.4 px; it is clearly visible only at 1080p and above, or on bright areas.
The matte bars get the vignette (spec order), so they read about (8,9,14) near the screen edges instead of exactly #0a0b10.
Medium/Low setQuality and setSize were only exercised in the harness cycle test, not inside the integrated app; dynamic-resolution churn (many setSize calls) was not soak-tested.
